claims: Tiger Woods was arrested for his first DUI on May 29, 2017, in Jupiter, Florida.
Police found Tiger Woods asleep in his running car stopped in a lane.
Tiger Woods had a 0.00 breathalyzer test.
Tiger Woods stated it was an "unexpected reaction" to prescribed medications (Vicodin, Xanax, etc.).
The arrest occurred around 3 a.m. in Jupiter, Florida.
Police found Tiger Woods asleep at the wheel of his black Mercedes.
Tiger Woods' black Mercedes had two flat tires.
Tiger Woods' black Mercedes had damage to both bumpers.
A toxicology report revealed a mix of prescription medications (Vicodin, Dilaudid, Xanax, Ambien) and THC in Tiger Woods' system.
In October 2017, Tiger Woods pleaded guilty to reckless driving.
Tiger Woods' plea to reckless driving allowed him to avoid jail time by entering a DUI diversion program.
As part of the plea, Tiger Woods received one year of probation.
As part of the plea, Tiger Woods received a fine.
As part of the plea, Tiger Woods received community service.
The 2017 incident occurred just weeks after a spinal fusion surgery in April 2017.
The 2017 arrest is often confused with a 2009 car accident in Windermere, Florida.
The 2009 car accident was a separate incident.
For the 2009 car accident, Tiger Woods was cited only for careless driving, not a DUI.
